why: DETECT-PATTERNS-1: a storage or backup appliance is not the product's to move. Microsoft's v6/v7 Plan page, 'Storage and backup virtual appliances': treat machine-based storage appliances like network virtual appliances, and it names NetApp, Pure Storage, Rubrik, Silk, Nasuni, Dell, Cohesity and WEKA as examples. Microsoft has NO list of their images, so this is OUR OWN LIST, read from the Azure Marketplace image catalog - not a Microsoft list. The vendor approves the target size first, so the scan refuses the machine as outside the scope of this tool, the way it refuses a network virtual appliance (WORKLOAD-1).

source.kind: Azure Marketplace image catalog, read by this project
source.how: az vm image list-offers -l <region> -p <publisher>, in eastus and westeurope. First read on 2026-10-16 by a separate lifecycle planner tool; every publisher and offer pattern below read again on 2026-10-23 for this file, and each pattern matched at least one offer in the catalog that day. The WEKA gallery comes from WEKA's own deployment code (its Terraform module for Azure): WEKA is not in the Marketplace. Offers differ by region and change over time.
source.drift: The catalog is not under this product's drift check yet: reading it needs an Azure sign-in, which the drift workflow does not hold for this purpose. DETECT-VENDOR-DRIFT-1 tracks it.

matchRule: A machine is a storage or backup appliance when (1) its image publisher equals a vendor's publisher AND its image offer is -like one of that vendor's offers, or (2) its Marketplace purchase plan (plan publisher and plan product) matches the same way - Azure keeps the plan on the machine when the image came from a gallery or a managed application - or (3) its image ID (community gallery, shared gallery, or gallery image id) is -like a gallery entry. Case is ignored. The publisher alone is never evidence.
proof: Not proven on a real appliance: each needs the vendor's licence. The fields themselves (image publisher and offer, plan publisher and product, gallery image ids) were read without error on test machines by the separate lifecycle planner tool on 2026-10-16. WEKA's signal comes from WEKA's own code and is not tested.

vendors.vendor: NetApp (Cloud Volumes ONTAP, Global File Cache)
Dell (APEX, Data Domain, Avamar, NetWorker, PowerProtect)
Microsoft StorSimple Cloud Appliance (StorSimple retired in 2022)

galleries.note: WEKA's Terraform module builds its storage machines AND its client machines from this gallery. Both are refused: the WEKA client depends on the network adapter, and a v6 or v7 move changes it.

notAppliances: IBM offers other than Storage Virtualize
